cringe: The unrelated RecipeFix pitch in the caption makes it feel like an ad tacked onto a food-fact post.
The 3-second countdown before every reveal feels like engagement-bait and gets repetitive fast.
Static versus screens sit almost unchanged for several seconds, which feels templated rather than edited for social pacing.
The tiny source text and small explanatory callouts are hard to read on mobile.

would_leave_at: around 3.0 s, when the first matchup still has not revealed anything
first_impression: Clean-looking nutrition trivia, but it moves way too slowly and feels like a Canva template with an ad CTA bolted on.
problems: The hook is not strong enough visually; the cover is neat but not surprising or human enough to stop a fast scroll.
Each question takes about 10 seconds, which is far too long for a simple this-or-that fact.
The countdowns add dead time instead of tension; viewers understand the format immediately and do not need 3 seconds per round.
The layout repeats almost identically three times, making the video feel longer than it is.
The actual useful information is delayed, while the reveal cards are only on screen briefly compared with the waiting time.
Some typography is too small, especially “per 100 g,” source text, and the explanatory notes.
The final summary is useful but appears after 29 seconds, when many viewers will already be gone.
The caption’s RecipeFix promotion is disconnected from the content and lowers trust.
No food imagery, texture, hands, or real-world context makes it feel abstract and slightly sterile.
The post does not give viewers much reason to comment, save, or share beyond mild trivia value.
fixes: Cut the whole piece to 10–14 seconds total: 2 seconds question, immediate reveal, then move on.
Remove the countdowns or replace them with a quick animated tap/choice moment under 0.5 seconds.
Open with the strongest surprise: “Ketchup has 2x the sugar of cola per 100g” or “A potato beats a banana for potassium.”
Show the answer faster on the first frame or use a cover like “3 food facts people usually get wrong.”
Make each round visually distinct with actual food cutouts or simple illustrations instead of only color blocks and giant letters.
Increase the size of the per-100g label and source note, or move the source to the caption and keep the frame cleaner.
Keep the explanatory callout short and large: “Red bell pepper: 2.4x more vitamin C.”
Put the final summary earlier or make it the last 2 seconds after quick reveals, not after a long wait.
Remove the RecipeFix CTA from this post, or integrate it naturally as a very small end-card only if this is an owned-brand ad.
Add a comment prompt tied to the content, e.g. “Which one surprised you most?”
Consider making it a carousel instead of a video if the goal is comparison and saving.
Check and standardize the USDA numbers so the values do not appear to change oddly during the reveal animation.
